description:
Coming off the best statistical season of his NHL career — a 97-point campaign — Kyle Connor once again put his scoring touch on display with a silky penalty-shot finish against Pittsburgh. description:
With an assist, Patrick Kane surpassed Mike Modano for the most points ever recorded by a U.S.-born player in NHL history. Midway through the game, Kane helped drive the play that led to Ben Chiarot’s goal, earning the secondary assist and securing his 1,375th career NHL point — a number that now stands alone among American-born players.  
Regarded as one of the greatest, if not the greatest, U.S.-born players in league history, Kane’s record is a reflection of his sustained excellence, elite playmaking ability, and championship pedigree. From dynamic offensive seasons to clutch postseason performances, this latest milestone further solidifies his legacy as a defining figure in American hockey history.

description:
On October 18, 2025, Mark Scheifele etched his name atop the franchise record books, scoring his 813th career point to become the all-time points leader in Winnipeg Jets history. The milestone came on a power-play goal, as Scheifele ripped a one-timer to open the scoring in the game. Fittingly, Scheifele was the franchise’s first-ever draft pick after relocating from Atlanta, selected seventh overall in the 2011 NHL Draft. His achievement stands as a testament to his consistency, leadership, and lasting impact on the Jets organization.

description:
Starting with a regroup deep in the Bruins’ end, Boston breaks out clean and the play eventually springs David Pastrnak all alone. He flies in on the breakaway, pulls off a slick deke, and slides home his 400th career NHL goal—doing it against Toronto, one of Boston’s oldest rivals, and sealing what would stand as the game-winner. Pastrnak later added another goal to cap off a three-point night and power Boston to the win.  
With the milestone, Pastrnak becomes just the sixth player in Bruins history to hit the 400-goal plateau, joining franchise legends Johnny Bucyk, Phil Esposito, Patrice Bergeron, Brad Marchand, and Rick Middleton.

A Stanley Cup champion and a key member of Team USA at the 4 Nations Face-Off, Guentzel continues to be a major impact player everywhere he goes.

description:
Since the start of the 2022–23 season—his first full year in the NHL—no one has scored more goals for the Canadiens, including game-winners, than Cole Caufield. A natural finisher with a flair for clutch moments, he continues to light up the Bell Centre. Down a goal late against Nashville, Lane Hutson blocked an empty-net attempt and pushed the puck ahead to Caufield at the far blue line. Caufield skated in and ripped a wrist shot home to tie it with 20 seconds left. Then, in overtime, he struck again—burying a feed from Nick Suzuki with just two seconds on the clock to send the Montreal crowd into a frenzy.
